title: True and Specific
author: Josue Valles
summary: Josue Valles argues that personal branding is not posting on social media but shaping what other people believe about you, which you control only indirectly through the work you do, how you do it and what you say no to. He uses Christopher Nolan, who has no social media yet commands huge budgets because studios believe in his work. A good brand, he says, is both true, matching your real caliber, and specific, fitting you and almost nobody else. He warns that posting generic content or acting against your stated values can make the belief worse. His practical advice is to ask a few people who know your work how they would describe you to a friend and, if the answer is generic or undersells you, fix it through the work you take on before posting more.
points: A personal brand is the belief people hold about you, and you can only shape it through your work, your refusals and how you treat people.
Christopher Nolan shows that a strong reputation can rest almost entirely on the work and the choices behind it, without social media.
A brand works when it is true, which prevents both undersold opportunities and collapse under scrutiny, and specific, which separates you from thousands of peers.
Generic content or actions that contradict your stated values can damage the belief you are trying to build.
To test your brand, ask a few colleagues how they would describe you to a friend, and fix gaps through the work you take on.
quotes: The first principle of personal branding is this: You can’t build a personal brand. You can only control the initial conditions that shape what people believe about you…the work you do, how you do it and what you say no to.

But people also pay attention to how you do things. They notice what you say no to, how you treat people, and whether you live up to your values, keep your word, and follow through on the small stuff.

If everything you write sounds like everyone else, the people reading it will assume you’re like everyone else. If you say you believe something and do the opposite, people will assume you don’t truly believe it.
True means it matches who you are and reflects the true caliber of your work. If people believe less than what’s there, you get smaller opportunities than you deserve.
That’s how a brand turns into leverage: people say yes to your next thing before they’ve seen it.
If what they say could describe thousands of other people, like “a great consultant,” or if it sells your work short, posting more won’t fix that.
